Detail

San Diego Padres @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

This one's near the top of the pile for watchability, pairing a playoff-race gut-punch with the two best arms either roster can offer. The Padres just took sole possession of the NL wild-card lead by beating the Dodgers 5-1 behind a Manny Machado three-RBI game, snapping LA's 11-game home winning streak, so there's real juice left even with the Dodgers' division title already banked. Glasnow is the headline arm here, sitting at a 9.19 pNERD (well above today's 5.96 average) thanks to elite strikeout stuff and a barely-there xFIP-, and he's doing it in just his 13th start of the season after battling injuries — durability, not dominance, has been the question mark. Pivetta, making only his eighth start for similar reasons, still brings a strong xFIP- of his own. Both bullpens grade out well statistically, and San Diego's pen has Mason Miller, who has 37 saves and a 1.19 ERA, lurking if it stays close. With a gNERD of 17.24 comfortably above both the historical and today's averages, this is one of the better watches on the board.

Tampa Bay Rays @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

A season-finale AL East tune-up that still has one genuinely great pitching performance to watch. Cam Schlittler has quietly authored an ace-caliber campaign for the Yankees, and both teams have already locked up their postseason fates, so this is more showcase than survival — but Schlittler's stuff makes it worth tuning in regardless.

Schlittler's pNERD of 10.82 sits well above today's field (average 5.96, ranking near the historical 95th percentile), and it's earned: his four-seam fastball sits at 98.0 mph with a .232 xwOBA against and 31.5% whiff rate, backed by a curveball that generates a 41.7% whiff rate. He's been the best pitcher in the American League by ERA this season, sitting at 1.94 with a 14-6 record — though he's reportedly lined up for Tuesday's wild-card game, so a short leash is possible. Seymour is no slouch either (pNERD 8.85), riding elite xFIP-, but he's an ERA over 5.00 across his past five appearances. The Yankees' offense (tNERD 7.38) brings serious thump, especially second in xwOBA and first in barrel rate against left-handed pitching. With a gNERD of 15.78, comfortably above the daily and historical averages, this one's worth your remote — just don't expect either bullpen to stick around long.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:05p

Summary

A rookie surprise start makes this one worth catching, even with both teams mostly playing out playoff seeding rather than fighting for their lives. Andrew Painter, Philadelphia's prized 23-year-old, has scuffled to a 5.59 ERA this season, but his pNERD of 7.72 comes from real stuff underneath — mid-90s velocity, a young arm, and a hefty positive luck score suggesting his results should be better than they've looked. Milwaukee counters with Shane Drohan, who's quietly been effective in his rookie campaign and carries his own solid 6.86 pNERD, making this an above-average arms matchup for a Thursday afternoon. The bigger story is context: the Brewers already own baseball's best record and clinched at 99 wins the night before, while the Phillies are still jockeying for wild-card position after failing to clinch behind Aaron Nola's implosion. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.92 reflects a genuinely fun, athletic roster — strong baserunning, bullpen, and a young lineup — while Philadelphia's offense has been a season-long liability. At 14.60, the gNERD lands comfortably above today's average of 11.79, making this a solidly watchable game.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

Skenes brings a Cy Young pedigree but has quietly labored through a down year, and this finale carries genuine late-season stakes for both fading clubs, which makes it worth a look even outside the shiny NERD number. This is the highest-rated matchup on the board today by a comfortable margin, and Skenes is the reason: his 9.82 pNERD is well above average even in a season where Skenes will attempt to help the Pirates secure their first non-losing season since 2018. The stat line undersells him a bit — his xFIP- sits at just 81, and a mid-90s heater with excellent whiff rates still make him must-watch when he's on, even though Skenes arrives at this contest in subpar form, allowing five earned runs or more in two of his last four starts. Opposite him, Kyle Leahy has been a solid, unglamorous complement (5.78 pNERD) despite struggling recently, allowing five earned runs or more in two of his last three starts. Team-wise, Pittsburgh's 7.60 tNERD outpaces St. Louis's 5.70, fueled by a lively bullpen and baserunning, while the Cardinals lean on youth and D but have been unlucky at the plate. Both teams are playing out the string, but St. Louis is trying to win for the third time in four games and needs to sweep its remaining games to avoid a second straight losing season — so there's at least a sliver of desperation on both sides.

Miami Marlins @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

Miami has taken the first two games of this series at Wrigley, and the Cubs are trying to avoid a home sweep in their final regular-season home series, which gives this getaway-day finale some late-September stakes even with both clubs' playoff pictures mostly settled. The Cubs bring the far stronger roster to the table, with elite fielding and batting numbers pushing their tNERD to 10.42 (well above today's 5.91 average), while Miami's tNERD checks in a shade lower at 9.05, boosted mostly by baserunning and a young, cheap roster that's quietly underperforming its luck-adjusted expectations. On the mound, neither Tyler Phillips nor Matthew Boyd is a marquee arm — Phillips has not reached the fifth in either of his last two turns, and neither exit followed a blowup — Miami simply took the ball — which puts a thin Marlins bullpen right back to work after grinding through extra innings and a bullpen game earlier in the series. Boyd, meanwhile, is fresh off a strong performance against Cincinnati, allowing just a single earned run on two hits in 5.0 innings, though he's never faced this Miami lineup. With a combined gNERD of 14.25, comfortably above the historical median, this one's watchable more for its late-season pennant-race texture than any pitching duel for the ages.

Chicago White Sox @ Kansas City Royals, 11:10a

Summary

Good stakes narrative: White Sox fighting for division, playoff race with Cleveland; Royals eliminated but playing spoiler; series has been high-scoring track meet with 22-1 blowout earlier in season. Now write summary.

The White Sox are fighting for their playoff lives while the Royals are just here to spoil the party, and if this series is any indication, buckle up for some runs. Chicago sits a game back of Cleveland for the AL Central crown, and after Tuesday's wild 14-11 White Sox win and a 22-1 blowout earlier this season, the over has cashed in eight of the last nine meetings between these two AL Central rivals. David Sandlin brings real swing-and-miss stuff (his pNERD of 7.72 is well above average) but his results have been erratic — he allowed 14 runs across his last three starts, spanning just 15 innings, including five earned runs on seven hits in only four innings. Randy Dobnak, by contrast, is more finesse than power, with a modest 3.59 pNERD built mostly on a quick pace rather than stuff, and he was tattooed by the Pittsburgh Pirates last time out, allowing four runs, seven hits and two walks in just 3 2/3 IP. Chicago's tNERD of 8.60 stands out (youth, payroll efficiency, solid bullpen) against Kansas City's middling 4.43, dragged down by a rough bullpen but boosted by some positive regression luck. At 12.18 gNERD, this sits above the historical median and right around today's average — not a marquee game, but the stakes and scoring trends make it worth a glance.

Cleveland Guardians @ Boston Red Sox, 3:45p

Summary

The Guardians are one win from clinching a playoff berth, and Ranger Suarez is doing everything he can to make them wait, closing his season with a run that's been nails: the left-hander has been better than that recently, allowing two earned runs over his last 19.2 innings across three September starts, including a start where that stretch includes seven scoreless against Baltimore and a seven-inning, eight-strikeout outing against Kansas City. His 5.31 pNERD reflects a strong xFIP- and solid deceptive pace, making him the best reason to tune in. On the other side, Daniel Espino's 0.00 pNERD isn't a knock on stuff — this is an opener, and the Guardians bullpen is responsible for roughly seven innings. The stuff is real, at 14.85 strikeouts per nine — it's just a lack of traditional starter data for a former top prospect finally back after multiple shoulder surgeries. Both bullpens grade out well, and Cleveland's young, cheap roster construction (low payroll, low age) padding its tNERD to 7.06, edging Boston's 6.90. Boston's own tNERD gets a boost from a hefty positive luck score, suggesting this offense has actually underperformed its true talent — a little scary for Cleveland given they're clinging to a rubber match in a tightening race. At 12.14, this gNERD sits a bit above the historical average and squarely in the middle of today's slate — decent, not essential, but the stakes make it worth a look.

New York Mets @ Texas Rangers, 11:35a

Summary

Both teams are already out of the playoff race, but there's still a tidy little storyline: the Mets have swept the first two games of this series in Arlington, winning 6-3 and 7-2, and are trying to finish the job as the Rangers try to avoid getting broomed at home in their season finale at Globe Life Field. Kumar Rocker, once a Mets draft pick who never signed and instead landed with Texas, gets a bit of symbolic revenge duty facing his old organization — though his season has been rough, with 59 walks and 20 home runs allowed over 143 innings, and a September stretch of 14 hits and eight runs over 13 1/3 innings, plus just 3.0, 4.0 and 4.1 innings in his last three starts. Rookie lefty Zac Thornton counters for New York, and while he has no pNERD data available, reports note a 3.40 ERA and 1.15 WHIP across 14 starts, missing few bats but rarely walking anyone, which lets him work deep into games. The gNERD of 9.80 sits below both the historical and today's averages, with Rocker's short outings and shaky command dragging things down — this is a game for completists only, not appointment viewing.

Cincinnati Reds @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

A fading Reds team plays out the string against a Braves club that's already banked its playoff spot, and neither the standings gap nor the pitching matchup gives you much reason to clear your schedule. Cincinnati sits at 73-85 and well out of contention, while Atlanta enters at 93-65 atop the NL East and holds a 3-2 edge in the season series. On the mound, Tyler Mahle's tidy 3.81 ERA and stronger underlying numbers (xFIP- of 90, good for a solid +1.40 boost to his 5.40 pNERD) contrast sharply with Brady Singer, who's been rough lately — a 9.17 ERA over his last seven starts. Singer's peripheral xFIP- of 111 is genuinely shaky, though positive luck (+1.00) suggests some regression toward better results is plausible. Offensively, keep an eye on Elly De La Cruz, who's been the Reds' table-setter, against a Braves lineup anchored by Matt Olson and Michael Harris II. With a gNERD of 9.52 — below both the historical average (10.81) and today's slate average (11.79) — and modest team NERD marks on both sides (Reds 4.38, Braves 5.24), this one leans skippable unless you're a Reds completist watching the season wind down.

A meaningless-standings matchup salvaged by two genuinely nasty right-handed arms. The Angels (60-98) are playing out the string in Seattle, but Bryan Woo and Grayson Rodriguez give this game more juice than its tNERD scores suggest.

Both teams are duds on the offensive/fielding side — Seattle's tNERD of 2.23 and the Angels' 0.78 both sit well below the historic 25th percentile, dragged down by shaky defense (Seattle's fielding runs are a brutal -45.8) and lackluster baserunning on both sides. Bryan Woo carries a 12-9 record, a 3.92 ERA and a 1.08 WHIP across 167.2 innings with 167 strikeouts, and his 96-mph fastball and elite strike-throwing (0.87 and 0.81 z-scores) power a 7.87 pNERD, comfortably above today's average. Rodriguez has been homer-prone and hittable overall, but turned in his cleanest outing in weeks against Minnesota, going 6.2 innings and allowing three earned runs while he struck out four without issuing a walk, and his 96.2-mph heat still plays. With T-Mobile Park's pitcher-friendly reputation in play, expect a tighter, low-scoring affair than the standings would imply — watch for the arms, not the lineups.

Arizona is still clinging to playoff hopes, so at least one team has something to play for; the Rockies, on the other hand, are locked into their eighth straight losing season and just want September to end. Eduardo Rodriguez has quietly had a strong 2026 — 15-7 with 140 strikeouts through nearly 184 innings — but his pNERD sits at a modest 3.37, dragged down by a lack of swing-and-miss and a velocity that's cratered to 92 mph. Across the mound, Tanner Gordon's shiny ERA doesn't match his xFIP, and his 5.92 pNERD is propped up almost entirely by strong strike-throwing and some batted-ball luck that likely won't hold. Team-wise, this isn't close: Arizona's baserunning and defense give it a respectable 5.51 tNERD, while Colorado's punchless offense and shaky glovework leave it at a league-worst-ish 1.50. Detail

Miami Marlins @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

A high-scoring Wrigley matchup with genuine playoff stakes and two starters trending in opposite directions — one of the better watches on the board today. The Cubs (87-70) are locking up their October spot, though they coughed up an extra-inning loss to Miami on Tuesday, and Kevin Gausman gets the ball looking to steady things after allowing five earned runs or more in two of his last four starts. Still, his 7.42 pNERD reflects real swing-and-miss stuff and a strong xFIP-, plus some positive regression coming given his rough luck number. Ryan Gusto is the more interesting story: he arrives in outstanding form, allowing two earned runs or less in eight of his last nine starts, though his modest pNERD (4.04) suggests the underlying peripherals haven't fully caught up to the results. The Cubs' 10.42 tNERD is carried by elite batting and fielding runs — Pete Crow-Armstrong has 45 home runs, tops in MLB — while Miami's 8.98 leans on speed, youth, and a shaky bullpen. At 15.43 gNERD, this sits well above the historic median and near today's ceiling.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's playoff-bound machine rolls into Philly with a rookie phenom on the mound, and the Phillies are down their ace — this one's worth your evening. Logan Henderson, just 24, has quietly authored one of the better rookie seasons in baseball; he's going 10-3 with a 2.51 ERA, 3.30 FIP, and 107 strikeouts across 93 1/3 innings, and his 9.16 pNERD ranks near the top of today's slate. It's also his first career appearance against Philadelphia. Aaron Nola, by contrast, is having a rough go by his standards — a 7-10 record, 4.49 ERA, 4.78 FIP, and 169 strikeouts over 168 1/3 innings — though his xFIP- suggests some bad luck baked in, and his positive luck component here hints at overdue improvement. The bigger story for Philly: Jesus Luzardo, the Phillies' best starter at 14-5 with a sparkling 2.87 ERA, has been out since mid-September with left shoulder inflammation and won't return before the regular season ends. Milwaukee's tNERD (9.95) dwarfs Philadelphia's (4.71), driven by superior baserunning, bullpen, and a notably younger roster. Combined gNERD of 14.46 sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — tune in for Henderson, stay for a Brewers team peaking at the right time.

San Diego Padres @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

Playoff seeding is on the line, Yoshinobu Yamamoto is finishing an excellent season in style, and Robbie Ray is walking a tightrope every fifth day — this one has stakes and a real pitching mismatch worth tuning in for.

The stage is set: the Dodgers lead their division, but San Diego has pulled level with the Chicago Cubs for the top NL Wild Card spot, while the Dodgers are chasing the NL's No. 1 seed, so this late-September tilt carries real seeding implications for both sides. Yamamoto (pNERD 8.65, comfortably above the day's average) has been dominant all year — he's lasted seven innings in each of his three September starts and is 2-1 against the Padres this season with only three runs allowed in 20 innings, 22 strikeouts against six walks. His xFIP- of 77 says the shutdown stuff is real, not mirage. Ray, on the other hand, is the drag on this matchup: since moving from San Francisco to San Diego in August, he's posted a 5.22 ERA and 5.86 xERA in eight starts, with nearly as many walks (26) as strikeouts (31) — his pNERD of 0.76 reflects exactly that control problem. Both lineups are lively (Padres' bullpen and fielding numbers pop, Dodgers' Judge-less-but-still-loaded offense leads the league in batting runs), pushing the gNERD to 14.43, well above both the historic and today's averages — tune in for the stakes and Yamamoto, tolerate Ray's control issues.

Detail

Cleveland Guardians @ Boston Red Sox, 3:45p

Summary

This one's worth clearing your schedule for: a division-race pitching duel between two nasty lefties, with Cleveland trying to hold onto first place in the AL Central over its final six games. At 16.16, the gNERD score sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historic average, and it's easy to see why. Payton Tolle, Boston's 23-year-old rookie, brings a 10.48 pNERD — his fastball is up near 96 mph, his strikeout stuff is real, and he's fresh off the first immaculate inning by a Red Sox pitcher since Chris Sale's third career immaculate inning in 2021, plus a 14-strikeout gem against Oakland last month. Parker Messick isn't far behind at 8.38, an All-Star this year who allowed three runs over six innings with eight strikeouts in his last outing to push Cleveland into first. Both teams grade out roughly average on tNERD, with Boston getting a lift from a strong bullpen and a bit of positive batting luck suggesting they've underperformed their offensive output. Add genuine playoff stakes — Cleveland's opener of its final six regular-season games, with first place in the AL Central on the line — and you've got a legitimately compelling watch, stuff over standings.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

A late-September tilt with real stakes for one side and pure playoff-prep for the other, featuring one of baseball's best arms on the mound. The Brewers have already clinched the NL Central for a fourth straight year and are steamrolling toward the league's best record, while the Phillies are still scrapping just to hold onto a wild-card spot. Milwaukee's tNERD (9.89) reflects a genuinely fun team: strong baserunning, a shutdown bullpen, and a young, cheap roster that outperforms its payroll. Philadelphia's offense has cooled to middling territory, dragging its tNERD down to 4.68 despite a deep bullpen. The pitching matchup is the real draw — Dustin May is pitching on short rest after struggling on Friday against the Orioles, and his rest-limited outing (bettors are backing the under on his outs) contrasts sharply with Zack Wheeler, whose 8.37 pNERD is built on an elite xFIP- of 74 and one of the best swinging-strike rates in the game. With a gNERD of 14.63, comfortably above today's average of 10.77 and firmly in the upper reaches of the historical distribution, this one's worth carving out time for, mostly to watch Wheeler work.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Jared Jones's return-from-elbow-surgery arc has quietly become one of the better pitching stories in baseball, and today he brings the best pitcher NERD score of the day into a matchup with a Pirates team playing solid all-around ball. Jones, who missed all of 2025 after internal brace surgery, came back at the end of May and has been excellent: he has pitched 90 2/3 innings in his return, with a 4.17 ERA but an improved 3.50 FIP and a 28.2% strikeout rate. His whiff rate now sits in the 94th percentile at 32.5%, and he's even flirted with history — he's thrown 6 no-hit innings this year. His pNERD of 10.51 is elite, driven by a mid-90s xFIP-, a 98-plus mph fastball, and youth on his side. Pallante, by contrast, is a solid-if-unspectacular ground-ball innings-eater for St. Louis, with his pNERD of 4.43 held down by shaky whiff and strike rates despite good velocity. On the team side, Pittsburgh's baserunning, bullpen, and even some positive batting luck push their tNERD to 7.59, well above the Cardinals' 5.80, giving this game a gNERD of 14.17 — comfortably above both the historical and today's averages, making it one of the more watchable matchups on the slate.

DJ Herz makes his first big-league start since September 2024, having missed two years recovering from Tommy John surgery, with a June setback further slowing things down. Opposite him, River Ryan makes his Detroit debut after being traded from the Dodgers to the Tigers, along with two other players, in exchange for Tarik Skubal, and hasn't pitched in the majors since 2024 himself. Neither arm has meaningful workload data this year — Herz reached only 65 pitches in his last Triple-A outing, putting roughly four innings as a realistic ceiling — so both pNERD scores sit at zero simply because there's nothing to measure yet, not because they're bad. The real juice here is on the offensive side: Washington's tNERD of 8.37 is buoyed by strong baserunning and barrel rates, though a shaky bullpen drags it back down. Detroit's tNERD is more middling. With two teams that have already checked out of the playoff race, today's 10.91 gNERD ranks solidly above the day's 9.18 average — worth watching mostly for the novelty, not the stakes.

Seattle Mariners @ Colorado Rockies, 12:10p

Summary

A rookie fireballer's second big-league test against a Rockies club that's spent all September playing out the string. Kade Anderson, Seattle's third-overall pick just last year, gets his second career start after a solid MLB debut where he nearly lasted six innings but had his day ended by back-to-back solo homers, finishing with three runs, five hits and two walks allowed with five strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings. The 22-year-old, who was the highest draft selection by the Mariners since catcher Mike Zunino in 2012, comes with a hefty 8.30 pNERD, buoyed almost entirely by his extreme youth and a favorable early-career luck bump — worth watching if you like scouting the next big thing, even if the FIP-driven fundamentals are still just modestly above average. Across the mound, Tomoyuki Sugano is running a rough 0.68 pNERD, with strikeout and command numbers both south of average, so don't expect fireworks from Colorado's side.

The Rockies remain one of baseball's weakest offenses and defenses — bottom-of-the-barrel Batting Runs and Fielding Runs — while Seattle's own glovework has been similarly dreadful this year, per the tNERD components. Both teams get a "positive luck" bump too, meaning each has actually underperformed its skill markers lately, so regression optimists can dream. With a gNERD of 6.66, well below the historic average of 10.81 and today's slate average of 11.43, this game leans toward background viewing — worth a glance for Anderson's development, skippable otherwise.

Detail

Miami Marlins @ San Diego Padres, 5:40p

Summary

San Diego's playoff push meets Miami's lame-duck reality, and the Padres bring by far the juicier storyline here. With a gNERD of 15.56 — comfortably above the historical 95th percentile and near the top of today's slate — this one's worth your remote.

San Diego enters riding a hot stretch that has them pushed to 85-69 on the season and pulled into a three-way tie for the wild card spots in the National League, while Miami has already been eliminated from the postseason race, so only one dugout has anything at stake. Making matters worse for the Marlins, their bullpen is a genuine wreck — Andrew Nardi, Anthony Bender, Pete Fairbanks, and William Kempner are all unavailable. On the mound, Eury Pérez is the real draw: 23 years old, sitting 98 mph, and posting the best pNERD of the night (7.14) thanks to elite velocity and whiff rates. Casey Mize is comparatively unspectacular (pNERD 4.19), a fine innings-eater rather than a show-stealer. San Diego's tNERD (10.72) leans heavily on a dominant bullpen and top-shelf fielding — the engine behind their surge — making this a legitimately watchable pairing of contender urgency and individual pitching intrigue.

Tarik Skubal doing Tarik Skubal things is reason enough to tune in, even if the Giants' half of this game is a mystery. The Dodgers grabbed Skubal at the deadline in a blockbuster that cost them serious prospect capital, and he's rewarded them with exactly the swing-and-miss dominance you'd expect from a two-time Cy Young winner — his 11.96 pNERD sits near the top of the scale we track, and this outing marks his final regular season start at Dodger Stadium this season, pitching on four days' rest for just the second time this month. San Francisco's counterpart is a total TBD, contributing nothing to the pitching math and adding a bit of intrigue by omission. The Dodgers' lineup (8.52 tNERD) dwarfs the Giants' punchless 3.52, backed by real batting and bullpen strength, while San Francisco limps in as a team whose 64-89 record makes late-September relevance mostly theoretical. At 14.50, the gNERD clears both the historical 95th percentile (15.60) and today's average handily — mostly on Skubal's arm alone, so watch for the strikeouts and stick around only if the Giants can make it interesting.

New York Yankees @ Arizona Diamondbacks, 5:10p

Summary

A potential Cy Young front-runner takes the mound in the desert, and even without Aaron Judge in the lineup, this one's worth your attention. Cam Schlittler comes in carrying a 1.95 ERA and 228 strikeouts, and just passed Whitey Ford, Ron Guidry, and Jack Chesbro for the most starts with 1 run or less allowed in Yankees history — his pNERD of 10.96, built on elite xFIP-, 98-mph heat, and a hefty swinging-strike rate, is comfortably above today's average and near the historic 95th percentile. The bad news for New York: the Yankees are expected to place Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday due to a right calf strain, though the lineup still has Bellinger, Rice and Volpe to lean on. Brandon Pfaadt is the far less flashy pitching story, a league-average arm (pNERD 4.11) with a 3.77 ERA and 84 strikeouts giving Arizona a chance to hang around. Team-wise the Yankees' tNERD (7.46) outpaces Arizona's (5.58), fueled by New York's barrel rate, while Arizona's speed and defense keep it from being a mismatch — Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo's stolen-base game remains a weapon even when the offense stalls. The 14.06 gNERD lands well above both the historic and today's averages, making this a solid watch.

Hayden Wesneski (pNERD 4.01) is the more interesting story: he returned to the rotation in late July following Tommy John surgery, and his last three outings have been erratic—dominant one start, shaky the next. Both arms are being handled carefully down the stretch, so don't expect deep into games from either.

On the team side, Atlanta's tNERD (5.19) outpaces Houston's (2.66), with the Braves' strong bullpen and barrel rate offsetting shaky baserunning; Atlanta is also running notably unlucky, which nudges expectations upward. The Astros counter with solid raw offense but weak baserunning and fielding. A serviceable but unspectacular watch, elevated mainly by the Astros' division race stakes.

Detail

Miami Marlins @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

This one's got real playoff stakes and one of the better pitching matchups on the board today, making it an easy pick for tonight's watchlist. San Diego enters with a real postseason push, and Manny Machado has 28 home runs and Fernando Tatis Jr. has 170 hits, 91 runs, and 35 stolen bases, with Petco Park a fortress at 46-29 at home. Miami isn't just playing out the string either — 18 of their final 23 games are against clubs ahead of them in the standings, so there's spoiler drama in play. The Padres' 10.67 tNERD (among the day's best) is built on a stacked bullpen and strong glovework, while Miami's 9.05 mark leans on speed and a young, cheap roster overperforming its Pythagorean expectations — that positive luck score hints they've actually been unlucky given their skill level. On the mound, Nick Pivetta's xFIP- of 79 is quietly excellent, buoying his 6.91 pNERD, while Tyler Phillips brings solid velocity (95.7 mph) but a more middling profile at 4.76. Combined gNERD of 15.70 sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historical average — worth your evening.

Chicago Cubs @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:40p

Summary

Chase Burns is throwing gas and mowing down hitters, so despite two sub-.500 also-rans, this one has real theater to it. The Cubs' offense and defense are elite even in a lost-cause series, while Reds rookie flamethrower Chase Burns gives the game a top-shelf arm worth tuning in for.

Chicago is fighting for the top Wild Card spot and enters having taken their second consecutive series by winning two of three from the first-place Braves, with the offense scoring 15 total runs in the two wins. Their tNERD of 10.34 is buoyed by outstanding batting and fielding runs, though a shaky bullpen drags it down. Cincinnati, meanwhile, is playing out the string at 71-82, and has dropped nine of its last ten — grim, except that Elly De La Cruz brings a different kind of threat, with 94 runs scored and 26 stolen bases, giving the Reds' offense enough thump to boost their tNERD via barrel rate and a young, cheap roster.

The pitching matchup tilts sharply toward Burns, a 23-year-old with 97.7 mph heat and elite swinging-strike rates, posting the highest pNERD of the pairing at 10.38 against Holmes' more pedestrian 4.93. Burns is riding a dominant campaign into what's being called his penultimate start of 2026, in a shortened outing piggybacked by lefty Brandon Williamson — worth watching before the workload cap kicks in. With a 15.25 gNERD, this one lands near the top of today's slate.

Washington Nationals @ St. Louis Cardinals, 5:15p

Summary

A near-must-watch matchup buried in a meaningless series between two teams playing out the string, elevated almost entirely by a genuinely excellent starting pitching duel. Cade Cavalli has quietly turned into one of the better arms in baseball this year, backing an xFIP- of 75 with mid-to-upper-90s velocity and an ability to work deep into games — Cavalli is not only posting elite rate stats, but he is pitching deep into games, with eighteen of his 31 starts going at least six innings. Kyle Leahy, on the other side, is having a breakout of his own since mid-June, running a 2.15 ERA and 2.93 xFIP, though St. Louis has him on a short leash — he hasn't thrown five innings since August 18, and is already up to 135 innings after just 88 last year. Don't expect either bullpen to protect a lead gracefully; Washington set an MLB record with its 38th blown save on September 9, with a bullpen ERA of 5.09. The 14.03 gNERD comfortably clears the historic average and today's slate, so watch the starters and brace for late-inning chaos.

The Rays have clinched their playoff spot and, having won six straight, are chasing the AL East crown with a comfortable division lead, while Boston is scrapping for playoff positioning — so there's stakes on both sides even if the standings gap is wide. The Rays have won six straight games, already clinched a postseason berth, and currently hold a five-game lead over the Yankees atop the AL East. Watch, too, for Tampa Bay's Chandler Simpson, who boosted his average to .311 with two more stolen bases, giving him 44 on the season as he tries to become just the third player in 26 years to lead the AL in both average and steals.

On the mound, Ian Seymour is the story: his 9.08 pNERD is comfortably above today's average, built on strong strikeout stuff and a favorable xFIP-, and he's fresh off a start where he allowed just two runs on four hits and struck out 10 in six innings to beat the Astros last time out. Ranger Suarez counters with a solid if unspectacular 5.63 pNERD, riding a run of back-to-back strong outings, having allowed just one run over 14 innings in wins over the Royals and Orioles. Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

A late-season laugher on paper, but the NERD math says pay attention anyway. Milwaukee's Brewers, fresh off clinching the NL Central at a franchise-record 36 games over .500, are chasing a sweep in Pittsburgh, while a Pirates team playing out the string has quietly set a single-season home run record. The 18.44 gNERD sits near the top of today's slate (7.94–18.44) and comfortably above the historic 95th percentile of 15.6, driven by two lively lineups—Milwaukee's power-and-speed combo (tNERD 9.93) and Pittsburgh's surprisingly frisky bats (tNERD 7.08) despite shaky fielding. Harrison has struggled lately, giving up 19 runs across his last three outings, but he's dominated Pittsburgh specifically, going 2-0 in three career starts without allowing a run in 17 innings. His pNERD (10.55) reflects real swing-and-miss stuff and a positive luck score suggesting better days ahead. Dotel, just 23 and making only his second career start, brings a 1.36 WHIP in a limited big-league sample but nasty velocity that props up his 9.34 pNERD—worth watching for the arm talent alone.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Cincinnati Reds, 9:40a

Summary

The Dodgers can clinch the NL West today, but the pitching matchup itself is more "watch for chaos" than "watch for craftsmanship." Los Angeles is running what amounts to a bullpen game behind Justin Wrobleski, who's coming off two scoreless relief innings in Miami on Saturday, and Landon Knack lurking to soak up innings if needed. Wrobleski's peripherals still grade out well for a lefty just past his rookie years, with strong strike-throwing and a plodding pace that padded his pNERD to a solid 6.84. Across the diamond, Brady Singer has been a mess lately — since Aug. 20 he's pitched to a 1-3 record and a 9.00 ERA over just 25 innings, with 25 runs on 33 hits while issuing 14 walks against only 21 strikeouts in that stretch, so his 4.53 pNERD is propped up mostly by better luck than performance. The Dodgers' 8.07 tNERD reflects a stacked, well-paid roster with a strong bullpen and batting line, while Cincinnati's 4.96 leans on youth and raw power (strong barrel rate) rather than results. At 12.20, this gNERD sits a touch above the historic median and right around today's slate average — watchable mostly for stakes and volatility, not artistry.

Philadelphia Phillies @ New York Mets, 4:15p

Summary

A Mets bullpen falling apart in real time gives this game an actual watch-it-for-the-chaos angle, even if the pitching matchup itself is the headline. Nolan McLean, still just 24 and a season removed from his MLB debut, has quietly built a 3.24 ERA over 166.2 innings and comes with the best pNERD in this matchup (7.53) thanks to plus xFIP-, a lively 95.5 mph fastball, and a young-and-quick-working profile that keeps things moving. Aaron Nola brings the name recognition but a rougher season line — he's actually pitched much better of late, posting a 3.60 ERA over his last nine starts while allowing 3+ runs just once — and his solid pNERD (5.33) is boosted by positive luck, suggesting his ugly full-season homer total undersells his recent form. Watch for Juan Soto, who has historically teed off on Nola over the years, posting a .283 average, .391 ISO, and left the park five times over 46 at-bats. New York's bullpen is thin — Devin Williams and Cionel Perez are both on the 15-day IL, along with Robert Stock and Daniel Duarte, meaning four relievers are out, which could turn a tight game messy late. The Mets' 5.52 tNERD narrowly edges Philadelphia's 4.70, and the overall 11.54 gNERD sits a bit above today's average (10.84), making this a reasonably solid pick without being a must-watch.

San Diego Padres @ Colorado Rockies, 12:10p

Summary

San Diego's playoff push against baseball's worst team makes this more about the stakes than the pitching matchup, though there's some quirky history worth watching for. The Padres are locked in a real wild-card scrap — they hold a 3½-game lead over the Diamondbacks for the third NL wild card, just 1½ games back of the Cubs and one game back of the Phillies — and they're riding a 9-1 run, having bounced back from their lone loss by beating Colorado 9-3, a game in which Ethan Salas hit two home runs, becoming the youngest catcher in MLB history to record a multi-homer game. Michael King brings genuine quality (3.64 pNERD, solidly built on a strong walk rate and pace) though he's had oddly rough history in Denver — he's 0-1 with a 9.53 ERA in two games at Coors Field, including a 7-4 loss where he allowed six runs on eight hits in 3⅔ innings. Tanner Gordon (5.68 pNERD, boosted by strong strike-throwing luck) has been erratic, giving up four earned runs on 10 hits in just four innings in his last start. The team-quality gap is the real story: San Diego's 10.48 tNERD (elite bullpen, glove work, and broadcast appeal) dwarfs Colorado's 1.56, weighed down by miserable batting and fielding numbers. At a 10.69 gNERD, this sits almost exactly at today's average — watchable for the pennant race and Coors Field chaos potential, not for competitive balance.

entry.content:

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

The best pitching matchup of the day, wrapped in a division-clinching afterglow — this one's worth your evening. Fresh off popping champagne for their fourth straight NL Central title, the Brewers roll into PNC Park with baseball's top gNERD score today (17.74), and the arms are the reason why. Rookie Logan Henderson (10-3, 2.34 ERA) starts as he tries to push the Brewers toward the NL's top seed, opposing Jared Jones in a rematch of their August 4 meeting in Milwaukee, which the Brewers won 4-2. Henderson's a legitimately fun watch: he has issued only 15 free passes all season, and he has never allowed more than three runs in any of his 20 career starts. Jones, whose 9.87 pNERD tops the day thanks to elite velocity and whiff rates, has been quietly dazzling himself — he hasn't allowed a run in his past two starts, a stretch of 13 innings. Milwaukee's lineup backs it up, ranking near the top of the league in batting and baserunning value, with a young, cost-efficient roster that overperforms its payroll. Pittsburgh's offense is thin, but strong bullpen and baserunning marks keep them respectable. Two power arms, a playoff-seeding subplot, and a division champ still hungry — good stuff.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Zack Wheeler's return from the surgical table is the whole show here, and it's worth watching even against a Nationals team playing out the string. Wheeler, who had a rib removed to fix thoracic outlet syndrome after his 2025 season ended early, has been working his way back from the medical condition and subsequent surgery that ended his 2025 season, in his first big-league starts since being shut down in August 2025. The numbers suggest he's found his stuff again — his 8.28 pNERD is well above the historic 95th percentile, driven by an excellent xFIP- and a swinging-strike rate that's climbed into elite territory, plus mid-90s velocity that shows the surgery hasn't sapped his arm strength. Across the mound, Jared Simpson brings a pNERD of zero, meaning there's simply no track record to grade — a blank slate rather than a red flag. The Nationals counter with real juice on offense: standout barrel rate, baserunning, and a young, cheap roster that all push their tNERD to 8.56, comfortably above average. The Phillies' shaky bullpen luck and lower payroll bump drag their team score down, but with a 13.29 gNERD, this game sits above both the historic and today's averages — worth a look mostly for Wheeler.

San Francisco Giants @ St. Louis Cardinals, 10:15a

Summary

A rebuilding-year matchup redeemed almost entirely by an interesting pitching curiosity, not by the surrounding baseball. Anthony Molina brings a 9.61 pNERD—well above today's 5.04 average—built on mid-90s-plus velocity, a favorable xFIP-, and youth (24), though his 6.63 ERA tells a very different story than the underlying metrics suggest; he's a August trade-deadline pickup traded to the San Francisco Giants in exchange for Tyler Mahle and recalled up to the team for the first time on August 24, and has made three big league starts since the trade and has never recorded more than 15 outs, so don't expect length. Across from him, Liberatore owns a respectable 6.29 pNERD but comes in with a rough year, sitting 5-14 with a 5.53 ERA and 1.49 WHIP, and a 1.486 WHIP means baserunners arrive constantly, with 3.3 walks per nine inflating pitch counts—expect both bullpens to get plenty of work. The gNERD of 12.75 sits comfortably above the historical median (10.80) thanks almost entirely to pitcher scores, since team quality is middling: the Cardinals' 5.89 tNERD gets a boost from a young, cheap roster, while the Giants' 3.72 mark reflects a club that didn't go the way anyone in the front office intended and will likely lose 95 or more games. Watch for velocity and swing-and-miss from Molina early, then settle in for a bullpen game.

The pitching matchup tilts heavily toward Cleveland's Parker Messick, whose 8.10 pNERD is comfortably above average - he's coming off a 12-strikeout display against the Detroit Tigers on September 5 and has eclipsed his strikeout projection in 7 of his last 10 starts. entry.content:

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's magic number to clinch the NL Central is two, and Jacob Misiorowski's turn to pitch happens to fall right at the moment they could clinch it. This is appointment viewing: the game's top pitcher NERD score of the day belongs to a Cy Young frontrunner who could clinch a division title while touching 100+ mph, against a Pittsburgh bullpen game that exists mostly to survive nine innings.

Misiorowski has been, in the words of one outlet, "the favorite to win the NL Cy Young Award this year", sporting a 1.95 ERA and a 2.24 FIP with 236 strikeouts, and opponents are hitting just .156 against him this season. His pNERD of 14.73 is comfortably above today's field (max 14.73, average 5.46) thanks to elite strikeout stuff (100.6 mph average velocity) and a tiny xFIP-. Across from him, Lake Bachar is functionally a bullpen-game placeholder — Pittsburgh has used a bullpen game in that rotation spot led off by reliever Lake Bachar (1-3, 3.52) the last three turns through the starting order — and his 3.84 pNERD reflects the mismatch. The Brewers' 9.93 tNERD (elite baserunning, bullpen, and a young, cheap roster) dwarfs Pittsburgh's 6.83, though the Pirates aren't dead yet in the wild-card race and still bring solid baserunning and bullpen marks of their own. With a 17.67 gNERD, this sits near the top of both today's slate and the historical distribution — worth clearing your schedule for, division-clinch drama included.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Sánchez leads MLB in wins and is coming off a rough outing against Houston, worth watching to see if he bounces back against a Nationals lineup that's playing spoiler with nothing but pride at stake.

The Phillies are still clinging to faint NL East hopes while the Nationals are already eliminated from contention, but Washington's youth and aggression on the bases make them a surprisingly lively watch late in a lost season. Sánchez brings by far the better arm here — his xFIP- of 62 is elite, and his season line reflects it: he leads MLB in wins this season, off his worst outing since July after giving up six earned runs to the Astros. He'll need to be sharper against Washington, a team he's already beaten once this year in an August start. On the other side, rookie lefty Jackson Kent is still finding his footing — he carries a 6.59 ERA and a 1.83 WHIP through six big-league starts, with 23 strikeouts and 20 walks across 27.1 innings, and his strike-throwing woes show up clearly in his below-average pNERD components. The Nationals' tNERD actually outpaces Philadelphia's, powered by strong baserunning and barrel rates, but a shaky bullpen keeps this from being a truly high-end matchup. A solidly average gNERD day, elevated mostly by Sánchez.

Boston Red Sox @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

A late-season, low-stakes-for-one-team affair salvaged almost entirely by watching a 38-year-old legend still humming mid-90s heat. Jacob deGrom, five years removed from his last true ace peak, is putting together a genuine comeback season in Arlington — he's Texas's strikeout leader and still pumping 97.4 mph, backing an xFIP- of 72 that ranks among the best NERD scores you'll see all year (pNERD 11.40, well above today's 14.73 ceiling but still elite). The Rangers, sitting a game back of a playoff spot, need him locked in, and their bullpen and lineup (Josh Jung and Wyatt Langford heating up) give this game a bit of juice. On the other side, Patrick Sandoval offers little counterbalance — he's been hittable lately, having allowed four earned runs on 10 hits in his last outing, and his NERD profile (2.61) reflects a slow pace and shaky command. Boston's bullpen and a modest luck deficit push their tNERD to a tidy 6.67, and the Red Sox arrive playing meaningful ball even without a division race to chase. Watch this one for deGrom, not for the pitching matchup as a whole.

Atlanta Braves @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Both teams are chasing October, both are on winning trajectories, and the pitching matchup gives you a genuinely dialed-in Gausman against a crafty veteran trying to punch his playoff-rotation ticket. Atlanta, sitting atop the NL East with its magic number down to four, sends out Martín Pérez, who is getting another look as a candidate to start in the playoffs after throwing seven shutout innings in his last start against Tampa Bay. His pNERD of 3.16 is unspectacular — velocity and whiff rates are down for a 35-year-old lefty relying on funk over stuff — but he's quietly effective in results if not process. On the other side, Gausman brings real swing-and-miss quality (pNERD 7.14, strong xFIP-) even though his ERA looks bloated; he was reeling at the end of August but has bounced back over his last two starts, allowing only eight hits and 3 earned runs with eight strikeouts. The Cubs' tNERD (10.53) is elite — thanks to a monster batting-runs figure and standout fielding, offsetting a shaky bullpen — while Atlanta's roster skews older and unlucky. At 12.96, this gNERD sits comfortably above the day's average, and Pete Crow-Armstrong coming off a four-hit night doesn't hurt.

Chicago White Sox @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:40p

Summary

A tight late-September AL Central tilt with more juice in the numbers than the standings suggest, thanks to two scrappy, budget-conscious rosters and a fastball-versus-command pitching mismatch. Both clubs are hovering right around .500 as September winds down, with Cleveland (76-75) hosting Chicago (77-73) in a game that has real stakes for pride if not much else. The gNERD score of 12.22 sits comfortably above the historical average of 10.81 and today's slate average of 11.09, driven almost entirely by the offer of two young, thrifty, well-built bullpens rather than star power.

The White Sox's 8.39 tNERD leans on the White Sox's 194 home runs, which rank sixth in Major League Baseball, a strong bullpen, and one of the league's youngest, cheapest rosters. Cleveland, meanwhile, is scuffling at the plate — the Guardians have hit the fewest home runs in MLB action this season (143) and rank 24th in MLB with a .237 batting average — but they make up for it with sneaky baserunning and a bullpen that grades out just as well as Chicago's.

On the mound, Foster Griffin (5.56 pNERD) has quietly put together a strong season and owns a tidy xFIP-, though his fastball barely cracks 91 mph. Chris Murphy (3.69 pNERD) throws considerably harder at 96 mph with a healthy swinging-strike rate, but his xFIP- suggests he's living dangerously. Not a marquee matchup, but a solidly above-average watch for a Tuesday.

San Diego Padres @ Colorado Rockies, 5:40p

Summary

The Padres are riding an eight-game winning streak into Coors Field with a playoff spot basically in hand, while the Rockies are staggering through an eight-game losing streak and flirting with a fourth straight 100-loss season — so the drama here is almost entirely one-sided, and it's the fun side. San Diego's 82-68 mark keeps them 2.5 games up on Arizona for the final NL wild card, and Manny Machado and Fernando Tatis Jr. have been swinging hot bats all series, with Tatis already homering off Colorado's rotation this week. Buehler brings a respectable 3.62 FIP for his career and gets a healthy luck bump after some tough recent results, though his modest strikeout stuff keeps his pNERD score middling. Freeland, working with better command (a strong strike rate) and posting solid peripheral numbers relative to his ugly ERA, actually edges him out on paper.
